shortDescription: Poland's industrial output rose at a solid pace in August, supported by a rebound in export demand, but the increase fell short of analysts' expectations.

children: Poland's industrial output rose at a solid pace in August, supported by a rebound in export demand, but the increase fell short of analysts' expectations.
Polish industrial output rose by 4.3% in August after climbing 5.1% in July. Economists had expected it would grow by 6.8% last month.
Bank Pekao analysts said the disappointing reading could have been due to a lower number of working days in August, but "trends in Polish industry remain positive".

"The recovery in industry continues to be driven by investment activity, supported by rebounding export demand. The machinery sector (+12.8% y/y) and electrical equipment manufacturing (+18.7% y/y) stand out positively," PKO BP economists wrote in a comment on X.
"Higher metal prices (e.g. copper) led to gains in mining (18.7% y/y, compared to just 6.3% y/y growth in coal mining). Weakness persists in the production of durable consumer goods (-7% y/y)."
